title: The Strange Story of Christmas Island: Exploitation, Occupation, and Refugees!
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

keywords.def: Far away from cities or other populated areas.
A person who moves to work in a different area or country.
A mineral used in fertilisers for agriculture.
Send someone back to their home country.
A person requesting protection in another country.
Land under the control of a country but not part of its main regions.

sentences.en: Welcome to a special Thinking in English Christmas episode!
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听特殊的 Thinking in English 圣诞特辑！

sentences.en: Today’s lesson isn’t about Santa Claus, reindeer, Christmas trees, or anything you might normally expect at this time of year.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目不是关于圣诞老人、驯鹿、圣诞树，也不是你在每年的这个时候通常会期待的任何东西。

sentences.en: Instead, I want to talk about a place that literally carries the name Christmas: Christmas Island.
sentences.zh: 相反，我想聊一个字面意思带有“圣诞”名字的地方：圣诞岛。

sentences.en: Christmas Island sounds like a cheerful and festive place.
sentences.zh: 圣诞岛听起来像是一个欢乐而有节日气氛的地方。

sentences.en: Photos of the island show bright blue oceans, white beaches, tropical forests, and its famous red crabs that are often featured in nature documentaries.
sentences.zh: 岛上的照片展示了明亮的蓝色海洋、白色的沙滩、热带雨林，还有常常出现在自然纪录片里的著名的红蟹。

sentences.en: But behind the beautiful scenery and joyful name lies a far more complicated, and often dark, history.
sentences.zh: 但在美丽的风景和欢乐的名字背后，隐藏着一段更加复杂、而且往往黑暗的历史。

sentences.en: Christmas Island has been home to exploited migrant workers, brutal colonial mining operations, Japanese wartime occupation, and, more recently, Australia’s controversial refugee detention centre.
sentences.zh: 圣诞岛曾是遭到剥削的异国劳工、残酷的殖民采矿作业、日本战时占领地，以及更近期的、澳大利亚备受争议的难民拘留中心的所在地。

sentences.en: So today, in this Christmas special, let’s explore why one of the world’s most festive-sounding islands has such a complex past, while learning some new English vocabulary!
sentences.zh: 所以今天，在这个圣诞特辑里，让我们来探索为什么这个世界上名字听起来最具有节日气氛的岛屿却有着如此复杂的过去，顺便学习一些新的英语词汇！

sentences.en: Before we get into the historical and slightly more controversial issues with Christmas Island, I think it is important to give you all some context.
sentences.zh: 在我们深入了解圣诞岛的历史和稍具争议的问题之前，我认为有必要先向大家交代一些背景。

sentences.en: Christmas Island is a small remote island located in the Eastern Indian Ocean.
sentences.zh: 圣诞岛是位于东印度洋的一个偏远小岛。

sentences.en: It is about 1,600 kilometers from mainland Australia.
sentences.zh: 它距离澳大利亚本土大约 1600 公里。

sentences.en: Actually, it is far closer to Indonesia than to the Australian continent.
sentences.zh: 实际上，它离印度尼西亚比离澳大利亚大陆要近得多。

sentences.en: Today most of the island is protected as national parkland and covered in rainforest.
sentences.zh: 如今，该岛的大部分地区作为国家公园受到保护，并被雨林覆盖。

sentences.en: Although geographically distant from Australia, Christmas Island has been an external territory of Australia since 1958.
sentences.zh: 尽管在地理上距离澳大利亚较远，但自 1958 年以来，圣诞岛一直是澳大利亚的一个海外领地。

sentences.en: This means it is governed under Australian law, but it is not physically part of any Australian state.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它受澳大利亚法律管辖，但在物理上不属于任何澳大利亚的州。

sentences.en: It is also important to note that there is another Christmas Island.
sentences.zh: 同样重要的是，需要指出的是，还有另一个圣诞岛。

sentences.en: The other Christmas Island is located in the tiny Pacific nation of Kiribati.
sentences.zh: 另一个圣诞岛位于太平洋上的微型岛国基里巴斯。

sentences.en: That island was named by Captain James Cook, and the two are often confused despite being thousands of kilometers apart in different oceans.
sentences.zh: 那个岛是由詹姆斯·库克船长命名的，尽管这两个岛相距数千公里且处于不同的海洋中，人们还是经常把它们搞混。

sentences.en: Christmas Island has a warm tropical climate all year round with a wet season and a dry season.
sentences.zh: 圣诞岛全年拥有温暖的热带气候，分为雨季和旱季。

sentences.en: The island is especially famous for its annual red crab migration.
sentences.zh: 这个岛尤其以其一年一度的红蟹大迁徙而闻名。

sentences.en: You might have seen this on the internet or on nature documentaries.
sentences.zh: 你可能在互联网上或自然纪录片里看到过这个。

sentences.en: The red crab migration is when tens of millions, really millions, of bright red crabs march from the rainforest into the ocean.
sentences.zh: 红蟹大迁徙是指几千万、真的是数百万只鲜红色的螃蟹从雨林向海洋行进的壮观景象。

sentences.en: Beyond the crabs, the island is rich in wildlife, coral reefs, and rainforests.
sentences.zh: 除了螃蟹，这个岛还拥有丰富的野生动物、珊瑚礁和热带雨林。

sentences.en: Today, Christmas Island has a population of roughly 2000 people.
sentences.zh: 如今，圣诞岛的人口大约为 2000 人。

sentences.en: Most residents are descendants of Chinese or Malay or Singaporean workers who were originally brought to the island for mining.
sentences.zh: 大多数居民是最初为了采矿而被带到岛上的中国、马来西亚或新加坡工人的后代。

sentences.en: You might be thinking right now, “Why is this remote island in the Indian Ocean named after the Christmas holiday?”
sentences.zh: 你现在可能在想：“为什么印度洋上的这个偏远小岛要以圣诞节这个节日来命名呢？”

sentences.en: The answer to this question goes back to the discovery of the island by European sailors.
sentences.zh: 这个问题的答案可以追溯到欧洲水手对该岛的发现。

sentences.en: The first recorded European sighting of Christmas Island occurred in 1615 when a British ship passed by the remote uninhabited island.
sentences.zh: 欧洲人对圣诞岛的有记载的第一次目击发生在 1615 年，当时一艘英国船只驶过了这个偏远无人居住的岛屿。

sentences.en: Uninhabited means that at the time no one was living there.
sentences.zh: 无人居住意味着当时没有人住在那里。

sentences.en: Although it may have been discovered earlier by people from the Indonesian islands, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 尽管它可能更早之前就被来自印尼群岛的人们发现了，也许吧。

sentences.en: For decades, the island remained unvisited and uninhabited.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，该岛一直无人问津、荒无人烟。

sentences.en: But in 1643, Captain William Mynors of the British East India Company landed his ship there, on December 25th.
sentences.zh: 但在 1643 年，英国东印度公司的威廉·迈诺尔斯船长驾驶他的船于 12 月 25 日在那里登陆。

sentences.en: In honor of that date, the 25th of December, he named it Christmas Island.
sentences.zh: 为了纪念这个日子，也就是 12 月 25 日，他将其命名为圣诞岛。

sentences.en: As I mentioned earlier, the island is often confused with another place of the same name.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前提到的，这个岛经常与另一个同名的地方混淆。

sentences.en: In 1777, so over a hundred years later, Captain James Cook, famous for being the first British man to visit Australia also named an island Christmas Island, after he arrived there on Christmas Eve.
sentences.zh: 在 1777 年，也就是一百多年后，以成为访问澳大利亚的第一位英国人而闻名的詹姆斯·库克船长也在圣诞节前夕抵达一个岛屿后将其命名为圣诞岛。

sentences.en: That island is now part of Kiribati in the Pacific Ocean and is completely different from the Australian Christmas Island.
sentences.zh: 那个岛现在是太平洋基里巴斯的一部分，与澳大利亚的圣诞岛完全不同。

sentences.en: For most of the 18th and 19th centuries, Christmas Island was still an uninhabited island far from anywhere else.
sentences.zh: 在 18 世纪和 19 世纪的大部分时间里，圣诞岛依然是一个远离其他地方的无人荒岛。

sentences.en: But, deep beneath the forests where its famous red crabs live, the British discovered enormous deposits of something called phosphate.
sentences.zh: 但是，在其著名的红蟹栖息的森林深处，英国人发现了巨大的矿藏，一种叫做磷酸盐的物质。

sentences.en: Phosphate is a very valuable mineral, which is used to make fertilizer.
sentences.zh: 磷酸盐是一种非常有价值的矿物质，用于制造化肥。

sentences.en: Fertilizers are used by farmers to improve the growth of their crops.
sentences.zh: 化肥被农民用来促进作物的生长。

sentences.en: And in the 19th century, especially the late 19th century, when the world’s population was growing rapidly and there was so much new technology revolutionizing farming, the global demand for phosphate soared.
sentences.zh: 在 19 世纪，特别是 19 世纪后期，当时世界人口迅速增长，有如此多的新技术彻底改变了农业，全球对磷酸盐的需求猛增。

sentences.en: The discovery of phosphate on Christmas Island transformed the island into an economic resource.
sentences.zh: 圣诞岛上磷酸盐的发现使该岛变成了经济资源。

sentences.en: By the late 1800s, the Christmas Island Phosphate Company had begun large scale mining operations.
sentences.zh: 到 19 世纪末，圣诞岛磷酸盐公司已经开始了大规模的采矿作业。

sentences.en: As there was no one living on the island, they had to bring in workers.
sentences.zh: 由于岛上没有人居住，他们不得不引进工人。

sentences.en: The Christmas Island Phosphate Company imported thousands of laborers.
sentences.zh: 圣诞岛磷酸盐公司输入了数千名劳工。

sentences.en: Most of these laborers were Chinese men, given the name Coolies.
sentences.zh: 这些劳工大多数是中国男人，被称为苦力。

sentences.en: This name reflected their low status and harsh working conditions, and I think originated from Singapore.
sentences.zh: 这个名字反映了他们低下的社会地位和恶劣的工作条件，我想它起源于新加坡。

sentences.en: One businessman Ong Sam Leong from Singapore built a powerful and exploitative system around the Chinese labor force.
sentences.zh: 来自新加坡的一位商人黄三龙围绕中国劳动力建立了一个强大且具有剥削性的系统。

sentences.en: In 1899, he secured a contract with the Christmas Island Phosphate Company to supply mining workers to the island.
sentences.zh: 1899 年，他与圣诞岛磷酸盐公司签订了一份合同，为该岛供应矿工。

sentences.en: His company had a monopoly over the workers and over the island.
sentences.zh: 他的公司对工人和整个岛屿拥有垄断权。

sentences.en: Basically, he controlled everything. First, he supplied the workers.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他控制了一切。首先，他提供工人。

sentences.en: He took workers, often from Singapore, and moved them into the island.
sentences.zh: 他从常常是新加坡的地方带走工人，并将他们转移到岛上。

sentences.en: He then started to sell opium and opened brothels and gambling dens on Christmas Island.
sentences.zh: 然后他开始在圣诞岛上出售鸦片，并开设妓院和赌场。

sentences.en: This meant that when the men were paid for their mining work, they would basically be giving back their money to Ong Sam Leong’s companies, either by buying opium from him or using his brothels and gambling dents.
sentences.zh: 这意味着当这些男人因为采矿工作拿到工资时，他们基本上会把钱还给黄三龙的公司，要么是通过向他购买鸦片，要么是使用他的妓院和赌场。

sentences.en: The laborers also worked long hours in dangerous conditions.
sentences.zh: 工人们还在危险的条件下长时间工作。

sentences.en: There were frequent accidents and no medical care.
sentences.zh: 事故频发且没有医疗照顾。

sentences.en: There were no hospitals or doctors on the island.
sentences.zh: 岛上没有医院或医生。

sentences.en: These conditions had deadly consequences.
sentences.zh: 这些条件带来了致命的后果。

sentences.en: In 1901, there was an outbreak of a disease linked to malnutrition and vitamin deficiency.
sentences.zh: 1901 年，爆发了一种与营养不良和维生素缺乏有关的疾病。

sentences.en: In fact, it killed more than a quarter of the island’s population.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它夺去了该岛四分之一以上人口的生命。

sentences.en: Christmas Island was drawn into global conflict during World War II.
sentences.zh: 圣诞岛在第二次世界大战期间被卷入全球冲突。

sentences.en: In 1942, Japanese forces captured the island.
sentences.zh: 1942 年，日军占领了该岛。

sentences.en: It became the southernmost point of Japan’s wartime expansion.
sentences.zh: 它成为了日本战时扩张的最南端。

sentences.en: Although the Japanese rule on Christmas island was harsh, it was not as deadly as many other occupations in Southeast Asia.
sentences.zh: 尽管日本对圣诞岛的统治很严厉，但它并不像东南亚的许多其他占领地那样致命。

sentences.en: There were beatings and intimidation, and women were forced back into the island’s brothel system, but large scale executions and mass starvation did not occur.
sentences.zh: 有殴打和恐吓，妇女也被迫重回岛上的妓院系统，但大规模处决和普遍饥荒并没有发生。

sentences.en: When the war ended in 1945, Christmas Island returned to British control.
sentences.zh: 1945 年战争结束时，圣诞岛恢复了英国的控制。

sentences.en: Then in 1948, the Australian and New Zealand governments purchased Christmas Islands’ phosphate mines and industries from the British.
sentences.zh: 然后在 1948 年，澳大利亚和新西兰政府从英国人手中买下了圣诞岛的磷酸盐矿山和工业。

sentences.en: This gave Australia a growing economic stake, an economic interest, in the territory.
sentences.zh: 这赋予了澳大利亚在该领地不断增长的经济权益和经济利益。

sentences.en: A decade later, in 1958, Christmas Island officially became an external territory of Australia.
sentences.zh: 十年后的 1958 年，圣诞岛正式成为澳大利亚的海外领地。

sentences.en: This transition was not smooth for the island’s residents.
sentences.zh: 对于岛上的居民来说，这一过渡并不顺利。

sentences.en: Many long-term inhabitants, often the descendants of the original Chinese and Malay laborers, were forcibly repatriated, forcibly deported, to Singapore or Malaysia or China.
sentences.zh: 许多长期居民，通常是中国和马来西亚原住民劳工的后代，被强行遣返，强行驱逐出境到新加坡、马来西亚或中国。

sentences.en: They were deported, they were repatriated, even if they considered Christmas Island to be their home.
sentences.zh: 他们被驱逐，他们被遣返，即使他们认为圣诞岛是他们的家。

sentences.en: Only in the 1970s did Australia introduce a scheme that allowed some residents more control over where they lived and their futures.
sentences.zh: 直到 20 世纪 70 年代，澳大利亚才推出了一项计划，允许一些居民对他们的居住地和未来有更多的控制权。

sentences.en: Throughout this period, phosphate mining continued to dominate the island’s economy, but by the 1990s the deposits of phosphate were largely exhausted, largely used up, and the mining operations were wound down.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，磷酸盐开采继续主导着该岛的经济，但到了 20 世纪 90 年代，磷酸盐储量基本枯竭，基本用光了，采矿作业也逐渐结束。

sentences.en: The population also stabilized at around 2000 people, mostly living in small towns or villages across the island.
sentences.zh: 人口也稳定在大约 2000 人，大多居住在岛上的小城镇或村庄里。

sentences.en: The end of mining on Christmas Island did not mean the end of Australia’s interest in the territory though.
sentences.zh: 不过，圣诞岛采矿的结束并不意味着澳大利亚对该领地兴趣的终结。

sentences.en: Instead, they came up with another use of Christmas Island… as a immigration detention facility.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们想出了圣诞岛的另一个用途……作为一个移民拘留设施。

sentences.en: From 2001 onward, the island was used as a remote detention center for asylum seekers arriving to Australia by boat.
sentences.zh: 从 2001 年起，该岛被用作一个偏远的拘留中心，用来关押乘船抵达澳大利亚的寻求庇护者。

sentences.en: If you arrived anywhere in Australia by boat with the intention of being a refugee or claiming asylum, Australia would send you to a remote island to be processed.
sentences.zh: 如果你乘船抵达澳大利亚的任何地方，意图成为难民或申请庇护，澳大利亚就会把你送到一个偏远的岛屿进行甄别。

sentences.en: They would not process your claim on the mainland.
sentences.zh: 他们不会在本土审理你的申请。

sentences.en: This was part of a government strategy to discourage illegal immigration, to discourage illegal arrivals by boat.
sentences.zh: 这是政府阻止非法移民、阻止乘船非法入境策略的一部分。

sentences.en: In fact, in addition to Christmas Island, they also used Nauru, which is a tiny country in the Pacific Ocean, which held asylum seekers to prevent them entering Australia and also Manus Island in Papua New Guinea.
sentences.zh: 事实上，除了圣诞岛，他们还使用了瑙鲁，这是太平洋上的一个小国，关押寻求庇护者以防止他们进入澳大利亚，还有巴布亚新几内亚的马努斯岛。

sentences.en: At its peak, nearly 3000 irregular maritime arrivals were held on Christmas Island, often in difficult conditions.
sentences.zh: 在其高峰期，多达 3000 名非正常海上入境者被关押在圣诞岛，通常在困难的条件下。

sentences.en: In fact, sometimes tensions erupted. In 2011, detainees set fire to an accommodation block, and in 2014 hundreds of people went on hunger strike to protest their treatment.
sentences.zh: 事实上，冲突有时会爆发。2011 年，被扣留者放火烧了一栋宿舍楼，2014 年，数百人绝食抗议他们的待遇。

sentences.en: The detention center was officially closed in 2018, though it remains ready to be reopened if needed.
sentences.zh: 该拘留中心于 2018 年正式关闭，不过如果需要，它随时准备重新开放。

sentences.en: The island actually made international headlines again in 2020, during the Coronavirus outbreak.
sentences.zh: 在 2020 年新冠疫情爆发期间，该岛实际上再次登上了国际头条。

sentences.en: Australia offered to quarantine citizens returning from China on Christmas Island.
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚提出将从中国返回的公民隔离在圣诞岛上。

sentences.en: Today, Christmas Island is a largely peaceful place.
sentences.zh: 如今，圣诞岛是一个大体上和平的地方。

sentences.en: It’s also often featured in documentaries for its unique natural environment.
sentences.zh: 它也经常因其独特的自然环境而出现在纪录片中。

sentences.en: It has tropical rainforests, coral reefs, and also that famous red crab migration.
sentences.zh: 这里有热带雨林、珊瑚礁，还有那著名的红蟹大迁徙。

sentences.en: You really have to go check out a video of the thousands, millions, of crabs walking through the streets of Christmas Island.
sentences.zh: 你真的得去看看成千上万、数百万只螃蟹走过圣诞岛街道的视频。

sentences.en: These things attract many visitors interested in wildlife and diving.
sentences.zh: 这些吸引了许多对野生动物和潜水感兴趣的游客。

sentences.en: The population is still very small. Around 2000 residents with a multicultural mix of Chinese and Malay and European heritage.
sentences.zh: 人口依然很少。大约 2000 名居民，融合了中国、马来西亚和欧洲血统的多元文化。

sentences.en: And although the detention center has been closed since 2018, it remains ready to reopen if Australia needs to or wants to accommodate asylum seekers or other arrivals on a distant island.
sentences.zh: 尽管拘留中心自 2018 年以来一直关闭，但如果澳大利亚需要或希望在偏远岛屿上安置寻求庇护者或其他入境者，它仍然随时准备重新开放。

sentences.en: Christmas Island is a tropical paradise with a history of colonial exploitation, forced labor, wartime occupation, and a controversial refugee detention program.
sentences.zh: 圣诞岛是一个热带天堂，却有着一段殖民剥削、强迫劳动、战时占领以及充满争议的难民拘留计划的历史。

sentences.en: Hopefully you’ve learned something new and found this episode interesting.
sentences.zh: 希望你学到了新东西并且觉得这一集很有趣。

sentences.en: Rather than a traditional Christmas special episode, I thought it would be more interesting to discuss a topic loosely connected to Christmas, but with a fascinating historical and political story.
sentences.zh: 与其制作传统的圣诞特辑节目，我觉得讨论一个与圣诞节若即若离、但却有着迷人历史和政治故事的话题会更有趣。

sentences.en: But what do you think? Had you heard of Christmas Island before this episode?
sentences.zh: 但你怎么看？在听到这一集之前你听说过圣诞岛吗？

sentences.en: Should remote islands ever be used for quarantine or detention?
sentences.zh: 偏远岛屿是否应该被用来进行隔离或拘留？

sentences.en: How do we reconcile a place’s natural beauty with its troubled history?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何调和一个地方的自然美景与其饱受创伤的历史？
